cohort: Live birth cases of Down syndrome (DS) diagnosed by the first year of life from the Registry of Congenital Anomalies of Tuscany (2003-2015 period), along with a comparison group of non-DS infants.
finding: Congenital heart defects (CHDs) are more frequent in females with Down syndrome (DS) compared to males, and this sex difference is more pronounced in DS infants than in non-DS infants, particularly for severe CHDs.
